sentences.text:
petitioner Fidusur Rahman has approached this Court seeking the benefit of pre-arrest bail,
apprehending his arrest, in connection with BI(EO) Police Station Case No. 05/2022 under Sections 120(B)/420/406/409 IPC.

3. Heard Ms. S.H. Bora, learned Addl. P.P. for State.
4.

The FIR unfolds that several fraudulent transactions, creation of void mortgages, irregularities in the documentation, misappropriation of funds from the loan accounts and conspiracies to defraud the Bank, all perpetrated by the petitioner has surfaced.
The petitioner is the Proprietor of M/s NAF NE Industries.
A Term Loan of Rs. 140.00 Lacs and Cash Credit of Rs. 58 Lacs (Total Exposure of Rs. 198.00 Lacs) was sanctioned on 26.08.2011.

Md. Arifur Rahman stood as personal guarantor and he created equitable mortgages of his land and building measuring 1 Katha 10 Lechas under Dag No. 317 (Old) 1656 (New) of K.P. Patta No. 25 (Old) and 66 (New) of Ulubari Mouza.

During the currency of the loan and after the loan accounts were classified as NPA, on 31.03.2013, the Punjab National Bank of Marbi Market Branch had initiated recovery proceedings under the provisions of the SARFAESI Act.

entities.text: Punjab National Bank of Marbi Market Branch
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: During the recovery proceedings, Anwaruddin Waqf Estate appeared before the DRT and stated that property of Md. Ariful Rahman had was transferred long before the creation of equitable mortgage by the vendor, who had purportedly sold the land to Md. Ariful Rahman.
This led to the complete break-down of the recovery process and it was found that the petitioner hatched-up a conspiracy with Md. Ariful Rahman and some unknown persons to defraud the Bank.
Further it was unearthed that the firm, does not exists at all and had used fictitious documents for money laundering with the current account maintained in the name of M/s NEF NE Industries.
The project was also abandoned in the midway, draining Page No.# 3/3 public money.
4. The petitioner has prayed for interim protection stating that the loan account was classified as NPA on 31.03.2013 whereas the FIR was lodged as late as 07.03.2022.

Earlier the petitioner was granted interim protection in connection with the case No. AB 570/2023 relating to an FIR lodged by the same Bank through the Chief Manager which was registered as BI(EO) P.S. Case No.
25/2022.
This interim protection was extended upto 22.06.2023.
It is submitted that the petitioner is unable to appear before the IO as he is apprehending arrest in connection with this case.

It is submitted that this bail petition would be infructuous if interim protection is not granted as the petitioner has already been enlarged on bail u/s 438 Cr.PC in connection with Case No. AB 1376/2022 and Case No. AB 1623/2022.
5.
The learned Addl. P.P. has raised serious objection stating that the case referred to by the petitioner may not be similar to this case as the case has been initiated by different FIRs.
To consider the bail petition Case Diary is indeed necessary.
Call for the Case Diary.
List the matter on 26.06.2023.
